Phone accelerometers are consumer-grade 16-bit MEMS sensors, sampled at SENSOR_DELAY_GAME (typically about 50 Hz); noise floor, bandwidth and dynamic range fall far short of a professional seismometer. This page reliably captures only obvious vibration — knocks, footsteps, a bumped desk, mechanical vibration; it is not sensitive to distant earthquakes.

Net acceleration = combined 3-axis acceleration - gravity baseline. The gravity baseline is tracked with an exponential moving average at alpha 0.01; slow tilts are treated as zero vibration — an inherent blind spot of gravity removal. Combined acceleration is independent of phone orientation.

Event peak, occurrence time and duration all come from real sensor samples; duration is the difference between the first and last above-threshold samples, and a single-sample event is shown as under 50 ms. An event ends only after 400 ms continuously below the threshold, so one vibration is not split apart.

A phone mounted rigidly on a hard desk or floor has the highest sensitivity; soft pads and clothing absorb high-frequency vibration. When readings are insufficient the page shows \"--\" and never invents data; 0.5 m/s² is only the default threshold — raise it in noisy environments.
